responses.evidence: One mechanism now separates the two cases, and it lives in exactly one place. B-04 gives the two new readers a distinct ABSENT status returned when existsSync(join(cwd, path)) is false and only then, with UNREADABLE reserved for a path that exists but throws on read and MALFORMED for one that reads but does not parse; it states that this deliberately diverges from readMutationReport (src/mutation-report.ts:190-204) and that readMutationReport is not changed, because a missing mutation report must still reach REPORT_UNREADABLE and MUTATION_NOT_RUN (#303, pinned by P-03 and by the existing [behavior:#303:B-08] case at src/mutation-report.test.ts:219) while a missing baseline or decisions file must stay silent. B-06 now keys the silent branch on the omitted-or-ABSENT input for both files and states the absent-decisionsPath outcome explicitly: no accepted label, every baseline label left as it is, no note. B-08 now keys both notes only on UNREADABLE or MALFORMED and says so, naming ABSENT and the omitted input as B-06's. The branches are therefore disjoint by construction, so no single input satisfies both a no-note and a note obligation. B-09 states that the call site probes nothing itself and passes each read result straight through, so the distinction cannot be re-derived in a second place. The distinction is observable without simulating a permission error: the absent case writes no file, and the present-but-UNREADABLE case puts a directory at the declared path so existsSync is true and readFileSync throws; the test plan and the DoD both require that pair per file, and the manifest's B-04, B-06 and B-08 observables assert it.

Each of P-01, P-02, P-04, P-05 and P-06 now names the existing test it retitles to carry [behavior:#304:P-0x] alongside the [behavior:#303:...] tag it already has, and the manifest's observableResult for each says the same with file and line anchors: P-01 -> src/afk-manifest.test.ts:203, src/logger.test.ts:1719, src/ship-gate.test.ts:2577; P-02 -> src/afk-manifest.test.ts:276 and :288; P-04 -> the describe at src/mutation-report.test.ts:659; P-05 -> the describes at src/mutation-report.test.ts:398 and :513 plus src/ship-gate.test.ts:2411, :2449 and :2487; P-06 -> the describe at src/mutation-report.test.ts:131. A lead-in statement in 'Existing behavior to preserve' records why one name can carry both tags: the gate matches each required tag independently with fullName.includes (src/acceptance-gate.ts:109-117, behaviorTag at :246), so the #304 tag is added rather than substituted and #303's own coverage is never removed. Retitling a describe carries the tag into every assertion's fullName inside it, which is how P-04, P-05 and P-06 are covered without touching an it. The Definition of done now requires a passing #304-qualified assertion for every id B-01 through P-06, and adds a check that retitling is the only edit those preserved tests receive: git diff on each shows changed describe/it name strings and nothing else, which is exactly the 'assertions unedited' obligation these behaviors carry.

B-04 now marks the shared-schema claim as this slice's stated assumption rather than settled fact, records that no sample incremental file and no schema artifact exists in this repository to confirm the shape, and cites the precedent for that gap in the code itself: src/mutation-report.ts:83-88 already records the report shape as hand-derived from the public schema 'because no schema artifact exists in this repository'. It then names the contained failure mode at the parser, as the clear condition asks: a differently shaped baseline parses MALFORMED, which B-08 turns into BASELINE_UNUSABLE with every survivor unattributed, so a wrong shape can only cost attribution and can never produce a wrong label, and an operator reading 'everything unattributed' next to BASELINE_UNUSABLE is one step from the cause. The manifest's B-04 'then' carries the same assumption and the same containment so the acceptance evidence and the contract cannot diverge.

B-07 now names the consequence it inherits instead of leaving the tension implicit: it states that the id-plus-file key diverges from B-05's location-and-mutator key deliberately, that the divergence is the recorded decision's rather than this slice's (src/mutation-report.ts:46-50 and ADR 0071 already commit the decisions file to the tool's own id, and amending that ADR is an explicit non-goal), and that B-05's renumbering premise therefore lands here as a stated consequence. The consequence is stated in both directions rather than only the safe one, because only one direction is actually safe: a stale ACCEPT entry either matches nothing, so its survivor is re-raised carrying its baseline label, or matches whichever mutant now holds that id in the same file, so a survivor no human adjudicated is labeled accepted. The harm is then bounded by what a label is - report text read by no gate, verdict or PR-open condition (B-12), with an accepted survivor kept in the list at full detail under the suppression non-goal - so the worst case is one mislabeled bullet a reviewer can check against the decisions file, never a hidden survivor and never a changed outcome. The manifest's B-07 'then' carries the same statement, and its observable keeps the id-matches-but-file-differs case that proves the ADR 0065 corroboration.
